title: Cardiac tumours, ventricular dysfunction and heart failure

items.question: What decides the effect of a cardiac tumour on the fetus?
options: Its type, and how it affects filling, function and rhythm
Whether it is seen on the four-chamber view
items.explanation: The effect depends on the tumour type and on how it affects filling, function and rhythm.

items.question: How do rhabdomyomas behave in pregnancy?
options: They evolve in the mid-trimester and regress after 32 weeks
items.explanation: Rhabdomyomas evolve in the mid-trimester but regress after 32 weeks.

items.question: A cardiac tumour is found in mid-gestation. What should follow?
options: Genetic testing, because over 60% of such fetuses have tuberous sclerosis
Repeat the scan only after birth
items.explanation: A tumour found in mid or late gestation should prompt genetic testing.

items.question: Which of these can cause fetal ventricular dysfunction?
items.explanation: Causes listed are primary myocardial disease, structural heart disease with volume load, outflow obstruction on both sides, and arrhythmias.

items.question: Which of these can cause fetal heart failure?
options: Mild tricuspid regurgitation in a healthy heart
items.explanation: Causes listed include ventricular dysfunction with inadequate preload redistribution, volume or pressure overload, arrhythmia, and compression of the heart.
